sourcedFrom: FULL NELSON BY Q™ 7.62MM DIRECT THREAD SILENCER / HALF NELSON BY Q™ 7.62MM DIRECT THREAD SILENCER — REV 1.0 (2021)
cleanIntro: Q's long 7.62 direct-thread can: 8.9 inches, 1.75 in diameter, 16.6 oz of titanium, threaded 5/8-24 straight onto the barrel with no brake or adapter in between. Because it is direct thread, the install torque depends on what your barrel's shoulder looks like — and Q gives two different numbers for that. The sheet covers the Full Nelson and the Half Nelson together and Q calls them the Nelson Bros.; the ratings are shared, the dimensions and the sound figures are not.

steps.title: Clear the host, bolt locked to the rear
steps.action: Magazine out, bolt locked back, then inspect the chamber and magazine well by eye and by finger before the can is touched. Note Q's wording here is stricter than on its fast-attach sheet — it names the BOLT LOCKED TO THE REAR specifically, not just an open action.
steps.prose: Unthreading a direct-thread can is a two-handed twist against a rifle you are bracing. Do it on a gun that has already been proved empty.
steps.quote: BEFORE REMOVING ANY SILENCER FROM ITS HOST, REMOVE THE MAGAZINE FROM YOUR FIREARM, MAKE SURE THE BOLT IS LOCKED TO THE REAR AND THE FIREARM IS UNLOADED BY PERFORMING A PHYSICAL AND VISUAL INSPECTION OF THE CHAMBER AND MAGAZINE WELL.
steps.cite: FULL NELSON BY Q™ 7.62MM DIRECT THREAD SILENCER / HALF NELSON BY Q™ 7.62MM DIRECT THREAD SILENCER — REV 1.0 — REMOVAL, p.1
steps.warn: Bolt locked to the rear, then look AND feel.

steps.title: The FINE PRINT sheet is the other half of this document
steps.action: Q requires this sheet and the accompanying FINE PRINT sheet to be read together before the can is used, and this one escalates the consequence wording to include death. Nothing here tells you how to clear your rifle — that lives in the host firearm's own manual, and this sheet only documents the suppressor.
steps.prose: The two-document arrangement is Q's, not ours. If the FINE PRINT sheet is missing from the box, it is missing from the instructions.
steps.caution: Two sheets ship with this can.
steps.quote: BEFORE USING THIS SILENCER: BE CERTAIN YOU HAVE READ AND UNDERSTAND THIS MANUAL AND THE  ACCOMPANYING “FINE PRINT” SHEET.
steps.cite: FULL NELSON BY Q™ 7.62MM DIRECT THREAD SILENCER / HALF NELSON BY Q™ 7.62MM DIRECT THREAD SILENCER — REV 1.0 — LAWYER SHIT, p.1

steps.title: Full Nelson ceiling — 7.62mm and smaller projectiles
steps.action: Check the host bore against the rating. Q rates the Nelson Bros. — its own collective name for the Full Nelson and the Half Nelson — for 7.62mm and smaller projectiles only, and the SPECS block under the Full Nelson's name lists 7.62 NATO, 300 BLK and 300 WM. A larger bore is outside the design regardless of pressure.
steps.prose: Your can's own numbers on this sheet are 8.9 in, 1.75 in and 16.6 oz, with 121 dB on 220gr 300 BLK from a 7 inch barrel. The 6.85 in / 12.2 oz / 133 dB column belongs to the Half Nelson.
steps.quote: THE NELSON BROS. ARE ONLY FOR USE WITH 7.62MM AND SMALLER PROJECTILES.
steps.cite: FULL NELSON BY Q™ 7.62MM DIRECT THREAD SILENCER / HALF NELSON BY Q™ 7.62MM DIRECT THREAD SILENCER — REV 1.0 — LAWYER SHIT, p.1

steps.title: Factory SAAMI or C.I.P. approved ammunition only
steps.action: Q restricts the can to factory certified, SAAMI or C.I.P. approved ammunition. On a direct-thread can there is no adapter to absorb a bad round's behaviour — the bullet's path is set by your barrel's threads and shoulder and nothing else.
steps.prose: This matters most with heavy subsonic 300 BLK, where a bullet that fails to stabilise starts to yaw within inches of the crown.
steps.quote: ONLY USE FACTORY CERTIFIED SAAMI/C.I.P. APPROVED AMMUNITION WITH THIS SILENCER by Q.
steps.cite: FULL NELSON BY Q™ 7.62MM DIRECT THREAD SILENCER / HALF NELSON BY Q™ 7.62MM DIRECT THREAD SILENCER — REV 1.0 — LAWYER SHIT, p.1

steps.title: Wait before you put a finger anywhere near it
steps.action: Straight off a string, both the can and the chamber are hot enough to burn. Q says to wait a minute before putting a finger in the chamber, and the same applies to grabbing 16.6 oz of just-fired titanium by its flats.
steps.prose: Q's warning is aimed at the chamber because the clearing check comes first. The can is the same problem one step later. The manual prints an ellipsis inside this sentence; the citation is cut to the contiguous side so nothing is elided by us. Its other half reads: "THAT SHIT GETS HOT.".
steps.quote: IF YOU JUST FINISHED SHOOTING, I’D WAIT A MINUTE BEFORE YOU STICK A FINGER IN THE CHAMBER
steps.cite: FULL NELSON BY Q™ 7.62MM DIRECT THREAD SILENCER / HALF NELSON BY Q™ 7.62MM DIRECT THREAD SILENCER — REV 1.0 — REMOVAL, p.1
steps.warn: Give it a minute, or use gloves or a cover.

steps.title: Unthread the Full Nelson off the barrel
steps.action: Put a wrench on the 7/8 SAE flats at the REAR of the can — that is the size on the Nelsons, not the 1 inch used on Q's fast-attach cans — and turn counter-clockwise. There are also 3/4 SAE flats at the front for a can that sits under a handguard. Q's entire removal instruction is that one turn.
steps.prose: Do not grip the 1.75 in tube to break the joint. The flats exist so that the twisting load never goes through the tube wall.
steps.caution: 7/8 SAE on the rear, 3/4 SAE on the front. No strap wrenches on the tube.
steps.quote: 3.Righty tighty. The Nelson Bros. feature 7/8 SAE ﬂats on the rear. We recommend you use these for install and removal. They also feature 3/4 SAE ﬂats on the front for silencers installed under a handguard. You’re welcome.
steps.cite: FULL NELSON BY Q™ 7.62MM DIRECT THREAD SILENCER / HALF NELSON BY Q™ 7.62MM DIRECT THREAD SILENCER — REV 1.0 — INSTALLATION ONTO THE HOST FIREARM, p.1

steps.title: Your barrel's shoulder decides the reinstall torque
steps.action: Before it goes back on, establish which shoulder your barrel has, because the Full Nelson takes two different torque figures: 10 to 15 ft-lbs on a TAPERED barrel, or 25 to 30 ft-lbs on a SQUARE shoulder. That is a factor of two and a half, and neither number is safe on the other geometry — a tapered shoulder over-torqued to a square-shoulder figure is how a taper gets galled.
steps.prose: Q cannot resolve this for you and neither can this guide. Look at the barrel: a cone leading up to the threads is tapered, a flat face perpendicular to the bore is a square shoulder.
steps.aside: Quoted as the extraction renders it — the ft ligature is dropped from every 'ft-lbs' on this sheet. The other value in the same table reads '25 to 30 -lbs on SQUARE shoulder'.
steps.cite: FULL NELSON BY Q™ 7.62MM DIRECT THREAD SILENCER / HALF NELSON BY Q™ 7.62MM DIRECT THREAD SILENCER — REV 1.0 — INSTALLATION ONTO THE HOST FIREARM, torque table, p.1
steps.warn: TWO torques for one can. Read your barrel before you pick one.

steps.title: Clean the muzzle threads and the can's own seat
steps.action: With the can off, degrease and clean the barrel's taper or shoulder and its threads, and the matching features in the rear of the Full Nelson. Q ties this straight to alignment: fouling on those faces tilts the can relative to the bore. Use solvent-moistened Scotch-Brite or a brass or nylon brush and nothing made of steel.
steps.prose: On a direct-thread can this joint is the only thing setting alignment. A tenth of a degree of tilt at the shoulder is a lot of movement 8.9 inches downrange.
steps.caution: DO NOT USE STEEL TOOLS FOR CLEANING.
steps.quote: 3.At a minimum, it is also recommended to clean the barrel’s taper / shoulder and threads as well as the corresponding silencer features of any fouling. This will help with alignment of the silencer to the barrel’s axis, ensuring optimal performance.
steps.cite: FULL NELSON BY Q™ 7.62MM DIRECT THREAD SILENCER / HALF NELSON BY Q™ 7.62MM DIRECT THREAD SILENCER — REV 1.0 — CLEANING & MAINTENANCE, p.1

steps.title: Field strip complete
steps.action: The Full Nelson is off the barrel and that is the whole strip Q publishes. The sheet carries INSTALLATION, REMOVAL and CLEANING & MAINTENANCE and no disassembly section whatsoever — the titanium tube does not open. If the inside needs cleaning it goes into a copper solvent bath or an ultrasonic cleaner assembled, and it must be fully drained before it is fired.
steps.prose: Q's own position is that a centrefire rifle can needs far less internal attention than a rimfire or pistol can, because its own pressures and temperatures do most of the work.
steps.quote: 2.When removed from its liquid bath, make sure the silencer is fully drained before ﬁring.
steps.cite: FULL NELSON BY Q™ 7.62MM DIRECT THREAD SILENCER / HALF NELSON BY Q™ 7.62MM DIRECT THREAD SILENCER — REV 1.0 — CLEANING & MAINTENANCE, p.1
steps.warn: Solvent trapped inside a can is a bore obstruction.

deepAbsentReason: Q PUBLISHES NO DISASSEMBLY FOR THE FULL NELSON. The sheet has no disassembly section at all — its REMOVAL section is two lines about unthreading the can from the barrel, and the maintenance section's deepest instruction is to submerge the assembled can in copper solvent or an ultrasonic cleaner. There is no baffle count, no end-cap procedure and no internal torque figure anywhere in the document. Q's EL CAMINO and ERECTOR sheets DO print teardowns, so the absence here is a design fact about the Nelsons rather than an omission. No teardown is offered because none is documented.

cleaning.name: BARREL INTERFACE
tasks: Clean and degrease the barrel's taper or shoulder and its 5/8-24 threads with solvent
Clean the matching seat and threads in the rear of the Full Nelson
Solvent-moistened Scotch-Brite or a brass or nylon brush only — steel tools are barred
Re-establish which shoulder you have before choosing a reinstall torque

cleaning.name: EXTERIOR AND FLATS
tasks: Wipe the 7/8 SAE rear flats and 3/4 SAE front flats so a wrench still seats square
Check the 1.75 in tube for dents, bulges or fresh discolouration
Wear PPE — Q requires it for all firearms cleaning and maintenance

cleaning.name: INTERIOR (ASSEMBLED)
tasks: Submerge the whole can in a copper solvent or run it through an ultrasonic cleaner
Drain it completely — Q makes full drainage a condition of firing
Do not attempt to open the tube; no disassembly is published for this can

reassembly: Remove any muzzle device still on the 5/8-24 threaded barrel and clean and degrease the threads.
Start the Full Nelson by hand, clockwise, and confirm the thread picks up cleanly with no cross-thread.
Tighten with a wrench on the 7/8 SAE rear flats to 10 to 15 ft-lbs on a TAPERED barrel, or 25 to 30 ft-lbs on a SQUARE shoulder.
Do not substitute one torque figure for the other; they belong to different barrel geometries.
fncheck: With the Full Nelson torqued to the figure that matches your barrel's shoulder, confirm it has pulled up square with no gap at the shoulder and no visible cant. Sight through from the muzzle end and check the exit is clear and unmarked. A direct-thread can loosens under fire, so re-check tightness after the first few rounds and periodically thereafter.
